1697年出現調音踏板。1720年Jacob Hochbrucker在巴伐利亞製: Tuning pedals appeared in 1697. In 1720 Jacob Hochbrucker made a single-action pedal harp in Bavaria, which could only raise a note by a semitone. In 1801 and 1802 Sebastien Erard took out the double-action pedal patent in London, and in 1807 Charles Groll registered the double-fork mechanism. The concert harp appeared in concert halls, opera houses and orchestras in London, Paris, Berlin and elsewhere, and composers such as Händel, Mozart, Hector Berlioz, Franz Liszt and Puccini took it up one after another.

The fingers curve naturally and close towards the palm to pluck the strings; the right arm may rest lightly on the body, while the left arm is freer. A beginner first learns the three pedal notches: the upper notch lowers, the middle is natural, the lower raises; then comes practice in different plucking positions and strengths, to produce different timbres and dynamics.

It is especially important in Romantic and twentieth-century classical music, and also appears in the opera house and in symphonic music. The concert harp, also called the pedal harp, belongs to the harp class of chordophones, Hornbostel–Sachs 322.222. Its construction includes an upright pillar, a soundboard, a curved neck and a base with seven pedals, and it usually has 47 strings, seven to the octave, with a range of about six and a half octaves. The player plucks with the tips of the thumb to the ring finger, generally not the little finger; the pedals change the pitch so that the instrument can play in every key. It is used mainly by art-music players, as a solo instrument, in chamber music, or to play in the orchestra and the opera.
音樂廳豎琴的琴身由立柱、音板、琴頸與底座構成，但來源未載明這些部件的材質。發聲體: The body of the concert harp is built from the pillar, the soundboard, the neck and the base, but the sources do not state the materials of these parts. The strings, which produce the sound, vary with register: the lowest are copper or steel wound with nylon, the low-middle are gut, and the middle-high to highest are nylon; some instruments may be strung entirely in gut. The materials of the pedals, the linkages and the mechanism are not stated.
音樂廳豎琴通常有47弦，每八度七弦，音域約六個半八度，自C♭1至G♭7。發聲靠指: The concert harp usually has 47 strings, seven to the octave, and a range of about six and a half octaves, from C♭1 to G♭7. The sound comes from plucking with the fingertips, and the dynamics follow the strength of the pluck; plucking at the middle of the string is fuller, while near the bottom the tone is nasal, like a guitar. Seven pedals turn discs in the neck that grip the string with a pin and shorten its vibrating length, so that every string of a given name can be raised, lowered or returned to natural, and the instrument can change key. Unlike folk, plectrum or Celtic harps, where the levers must be flipped by hand string by string, it changes semitones by pedal, but it is still not a fully chromatic instrument.
